newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PRESIDENT LISTS DOUBTS ABOUT GOVT PROGRAMME.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PRESIDENT LISTS DOUBTS ABOUT GOVT PROGRAMME.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel said on Thursday that he was pleased that leaders of the ruling centre-right coalition were ready to face its economic crisis, but he had doubts over the way the coalition agreed to do it.

In a statement he said that while the economic stabilisation programme agreed on Wednesday could possibly resolve the immediate situation, it did not address what the government intended to do in the longer term.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus and leaders of the two junior coalition parties agreed on Wednesday to an austerity programme of unspecified budget cuts and public sector wage freezes and ministerial changes aimed at halting a crisis of confidence in the Czech crown and the economy.

In listing what he called "several doubts", Havel said the plan "still does not mention even a word about long-term programme aims of this coalition and government, and does not, in the new situation, develop and make concrete its programme statement."
Havel said it did not offer "even a word" of who was responsible for the economic crisis, and that he could not understand the connection between the personnel changes -- and the new programme.
Still, he said he indicated he would "could" confirm the personnel changes -- which included naming the education minister Ivan Pilip as the new finance minister -- on Monday.
